text: dsh-config-studio 是为 DSH 网页设置提供的插件配置编辑器。它在设置页列出当前 profile 中可寻址的 Loader 条目，并按每个插件的 Config schema 展示字段。用户可以搜索和分类浏览条目，查看继承值与覆盖值，编辑文本、数字、开关、枚举或 JSON 字段，重置字段并在保存前检查差异。保存由 Host 校验后写入 profile 配置补丁并通过 Loader 应用。适合需要在图形界面查看和调整 DSH 插件配置的用户；代码未要求额外 API 密钥或外部服务。

dsh-config-studio adds a settings page for editing DSH plugin configuration. It lists Loader entries and renders forms from their Config schemas. Users can search, edit fields, reset values, and review changes before the Host saves the profile patch. It needs no API key or external service.
我想在 DSH 设置页面里查看并调整已安装插件的配置。
能不能把插件的配置项做成表单，而不是让我手改 YAML？
How can I browse and edit DSH plugin settings through a web form?
dsh-config-studio 的功能「配置条目浏览」：在设置页列出可寻址的 Loader 条目，显示状态、覆盖情况和字段数量；支持按 id 或包名搜索，并按功能或来源分组。
dsh-config-studio 的功能「Schema 表单编辑」：根据插件 Config schema 显示可编辑字段，支持文本、数字、开关、枚举和 JSON 输入；用户可重置字段、预览差异，再提交变更。

dsh-config-studio README · Introduction：

dsh-config-studio README · Introduction：A settings page for the part of DSH configuration the built-in pages never reach. It lists every **addressable Loader entry** in the active profile, renders a form from that plugin's own `Config` schema, and writes the fields you change into the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` — through `ctx.configEditor`, the same writer DSH's own settings use, but without the `volatile`-only restriction.
dsh-config-studio README · Introduction：The page appears in **Settings → Plugin configuration** (设置 → 插件配置) and follows the Harness language (English / 简体中文).

dsh-config-studio README · Why this exists：DSH's built-in settings forms write through `settings.mutate`, which only accepts fields a plugin declared with `.volatile()`; writing anything else throws `Config field "<path>" is not volatile`. Everything else is expected to be edited by hand in YAML.

dsh-config-studio README · Why this exists：That restriction is reasonable for live-reloadable preferences, but it leaves most of a real profile without a UI: plugin lists, timeouts, feature switches, provider tables, and the rest. This plugin takes the other road — the complete raw config — and lets the Host validate and apply it exactly as the Loader would.

dsh-config-studio README · Features：- **Browse** — every entry `configEditor.entries()` returns, with package name, field count, override badge, and current status. Search by id or package; switch between *editable only* (default) and *all*; group by **function** (models, agents, tools, web, accounts, runtime, sessions, interface, platform, other) or by **origin** (built-in / third-party); collapse sections; the browsing state survives opening an entry and coming back.
- **Edit** — one field per top-level config key: text, number, switch, select for enums, and a JSON editor for objects and arrays. Each row shows the value in effect, whether it comes from the profile patch, and a one-click **Reset** back to the inherited value.
- **Review, then save** — a patch-shaped diff of what will be written, a revision check that refuses to overwrite a concurrent edit, and a result line that says whether the override was applied or removed.
- **Read-only by design** — credentials, `!!js` expressions, unsupported schema shapes, and oversized entries are never writable here (table below).
- **Bilingual** — English and Simplified Chinese, following the Harness language, including the nav label, e

dsh-config-studio README · Install：Published on npm as [`dsh-config-studio`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-config-studio), and also a plain `dsh.bundle` bundle with **no dependencies and no build step**. Every source below installs the same code — pick the one that matches your host.

dsh-config-studio README · npm (recommended)：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-config-studio
```

Replace `web` with your own profile name. Restart the host if it does not pick the plugin up, then reload the page.

**DSH Desktop** manages its own profile, so the command above cannot install into it: open **Settings → Plugins**, paste `dsh-config-studio` into the install box, make sure the plugin is enabled, then reload the page (`Cmd/Ctrl+R`).

dsh-config-studio README · Without npm：The same version installs from the release tarball or straight from this repository — useful on a host that cannot reach the registry:

```bash

dsh-config-studio README · release tarball (pinned to a tag, so the URL never rots)：dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/MaxHan0102/dsh-config-studio/releases/download/v0.1.0/dsh-config-studio-0.1.0.tgz
section: release tarball (pinned to a tag, so the URL never rots)

dsh-config-studio README · or straight from the repository：dsh plugin --profile web add github:MaxHan0102/dsh-config-studio
```

On Desktop, paste either string into the same install box.

dsh-config-studio README · Update：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-config-studio@latest
```

On Desktop, use the update control on the plugin's card. A tarball or git install has no update check — remove and re-add it with the newer tag or commit.

dsh-config-studio README · Remove：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-config-studio
```

Any override the plugin wrote stays in `cordis.patch.yml`; removing the plugin does not touch your configuration.

dsh-config-studio README · Requirements：| | |
|---|---|
| DSH | `0.2.1-rc.5` or newer (tested on `0.2.1-rc.5` and `0.2.2-rc.1`) |
| Services | `ctx.configEditor` and `ctx.connection.fetch` — both ship with the Web composition |
| Node | 20+ |
| Browser | any current Web GUI; the section is a normal client plugin |

The package deliberately declares no DSH version range: it is plain JavaScript with no host imports, so it keeps installing on newer hosts instead of being gated out by a prerelease peer range.

dsh-config-studio README · Usage：1. **Open** **Settings → Plugin configuration**. The first screen lists the entries that have something to edit; switch the filter to *All entries* to inspect the read-only ones.
2. **Pick an entry.** The pane shows its fields, generated from the plugin's own schema. A field marked **Overridden** comes from your profile patch; the rest show the inherited value.
3. **Edit.** Changed rows are highlighted; invalid numbers, enums, and JSON are marked before you save. **Reset** on a row marks it to be restored to the inherited value (the pending value is shown in the field).
4. **Review.** *Save to profile* opens a diff of exactly what will be written.
5. **Apply.** The Host validates the complete config against the plugin's schema, writes the patch atomically, and reloads the entry through the Loader. A value the schema rejects comes back with the offending field named; a concurrent edit comes back as a conflict and offers a reload.

dsh-config-studio README · What the badges mean：| Badge | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Overridden** (entry) | The profile patch has a `config:` record for this entry |
| **Overridden** (field) | This key is written in that record, so the value comes from the profile layer |
| **Read-only** | See the table below; the field is shown for context but will not be written |
| **Third-party** | The package is not under the `@deepseek-ai/` scope |

dsh-config-studio README · Two behaviours worth knowing：**A patch replaces the whole config.** DSH applies a patch by replacing an entry's `config` object, not by merging keys. Saving one field therefore writes the entry's current config plus your change, and pins the other values it already had. If every field ends up equal to the inherited layer, the record is removed entirely — that is what *Reset* means for a whole entry.

dsh-config-studio README · Two behaviours worth knowing：**Some changes reload the plugin.** Every save goes through the Loader's normal lifecycle, so the plugin restarts with its new config. A few plugins only take effect after the host restarts; the page says so in the result line.

dsh-config-studio README · Read-only rules：| Condition | Reason |
|---|---|
| `role('secret')` field | the value never leaves the Host — the page only learns whether it is set |
| `role('credential-ref')` field | a reference is not an editable value |
| An object with a secret somewhere below it | editing it as JSON could leak the secret |
| An unevaluated `!!js` expression | only YAML can express it safely |
| A schema type the form does not understand | no safe control exists |
| `meta.disabled` on the field | the plugin disables it |
| Entry larger than 64 KiB | too large to edit responsibly in one form |
| Entry disabled, failed, inactive, or a group | not addressable right now |
| Plugin declares no `Config` | nothing to generate a form from |

dsh-config-studio README · How it works：Two halves, both in this repository:

- **Host** (`index.js`) — three `POST` endpoints registered through `ctx.connection.fetch`, so the `/api` fence, Host/Origin checks, and cookie authentication apply before dispatch. It imports nothing outside Node built-ins: the form shape is read from the live `schemastery` schema the Loader already holds.

dsh-config-studio README · How it works：| Endpoint | Body | Answers |
  |---|---|---|
  | `/api/config-studio/list` | `{}` | entries, status, field counts, category, origin |
  | `/api/config-studio/read` | `{ id }` | revision, fields, values, read-only reason |
  | `/api/config-studio/write` | `{ id, expectedRevision, changes }` | `{ ok, revision }` or `{ ok: false, error }` |

dsh-config-studio README · How it works：- **Client** (`client.js`) — a `settings.section` registration written in the module-loader format, with no Harness client package imports. Controls are the plugin's own, styled with theme tokens.

dsh-config-studio README · How it works：Writes are validated twice: once against the plugin's schema in the request, and again inside `configEditor.edit()`, which holds the profile lock, preserves comments and `!!js`, writes atomically, reloads the entry, and rolls the file back if the reload fails. `revision` is a hash of the entry's inherited layer, profile override, and raw config, so a stale form is refused instead of silently overwriting.

dsh-config-studio README · Troubleshooting：| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| No **Plugin configuration** section | Confirm the plugin is enabled and active, then reload the page. On the Desktop app, check the plugin's card in **Settings → Plugins**. |
| "The configuration service did not answer." | The Host half is not active: check the DSH version, and that the entry is `active` in the plugin list. |
| A field you need is read-only | It matches one of the rules above; edit `cordis.patch.yml` directly for secrets and `!!js`. |
| Save succeeded but nothing changed | Another layer wins: a home patch (`~/.dsh/cordis.patch.yml`) or a `--patch` overlay takes precedence over the profile layer. |
| Save failed with a conflict | Someone (or another tool) wrote the entry after the page read it; reload the entry and re-apply. |
| The page vanished after a DSH update | Check the upstream release notes for the settings surface; open an issue with the DSH version. |

dsh-config-studio README · Security：- Only the active profile's `cordis.patch.yml` is ever written. Home patches, command-line overlays, and bundle layers are read but never modified.
- Only entries returned by `configEditor.entries()` are addressable; everything else is invisible to this page.
- Secrets are never sent to the browser, and schema error messages are scrubbed of credential text before they leave the Host.
- Logs carry entry ids and field keys only — never configuration values.
- The browser cannot pick a different write target: the Host rebuilds the candidate config from its own copy and re-validates it.

dsh-config-studio README · Development：The repository is the installed artifact — plain JavaScript, no build.

```text
index.js           Host half: schema introspection, endpoints, validation
client.js          Client half: settings section, form, diff, i18n
cordis.patch.yml   Bundle patch that inserts the Host row
locale/*.json      Display metadata for the plugins page

To run a checkout against a disposable profile:

dsh-config-studio README · Development：```bash
cp -R ~/.dsh/profiles /tmp/dsh-home/profiles
DSH_HOME=/tmp/dsh-home dsh --profile web --no-open --port 0
```

Link the working copy into that profile (`dsh plugin --profile web add <absolute path>`) and reload the page after edits. The Host half is reloaded by re-enabling the plugin; the client half is re-fetched on page reload.
